positions.text: MCP governance should be treated as a continuous institutional process, not as a sequence of static specification releases. Server behavior, tool permissions, and observed failure data should feed a review mechanism that can update rules while preserving an auditable record.
scope_conditions: MCP server discovery, authorization, tool permission, and protocol governance where behavior data and auditable review are available.

positions.text: An agent identity standard is incomplete unless it binds identity to a verifiable mandate, attributes action to a principal, and makes costly evasion of negative history part of the design.
scope_conditions: Standards for autonomous agent identity and delegated authority in systems that permit verifiable mandates and persistent identity.

positions.text: Agentic commerce protocols need a portable, verifiable performance layer that records completed transactions, disputes, reversals, and validated outcomes without collapsing reputation into a single platform score.
scope_conditions: Repeated agentic commerce where counterparties need portable performance evidence and transaction-level recourse.

positions.text: Agentic payment design must couple programmable settlement with bounded mandates, transaction-level provenance, revocation, and accountable loss allocation. Efficient settlement without institutional controls scales the consequences of error.
scope_conditions: Autonomous agent payments using programmable or stablecoin settlement where agents may act without transaction-by-transaction human authorization.

positions.text: Decentralized AI architecture should evaluate incentive compatibility separately from technical distribution. A system is not institutionally decentralized merely because agents, wallets, and execution are distributed.
scope_conditions: Decentralized AI and DAO architectures using tokens, distributed execution, or agent coordination.

positions.text: Machine agency governance must preserve action-level attribution across delegation chains. Architecture diagrams and policy statements are insufficient if a reviewer cannot reconstruct which agent acted, under whose authority, using which evidence, and with which downstream effect.
scope_conditions: Multi-agent or autonomous systems with delegated authority and distributed actions.

positions.text: DAO governance should be evaluated by explicit resistance to capture, participation collapse, and collective-action failure. Token voting is an input, not evidence that those failure modes have been solved.
scope_conditions: DAO governance systems using token voting or comparable on-chain collective decision procedures.
